data.title: Elopak ASA (OB:ELO) Will Pay A €0.065 Dividend In Four Days
data.description:
Some investors rely on dividends for growing their wealth, and if you're one of those dividend sleuths, you might be intrigued to know that Elopak ASA (OB:ELO) is about to go ex-dividend in just 4 days. Typically, the ex-dividend date is two business days before the record date, which is the date on which a company determines the shareholders eligible to receive a dividend. The ex-dividend date is important because any transaction on a stock needs to have been settled before the record date in order to be eligible for a dividend. Therefore, if you purchase Elopak's shares on or after the 15th of October, you won't be eligible to receive the dividend, when it is paid on the 28th of October.

The company's next dividend payment will be €0.065 per share, on the back of last year when the company paid a total of €0.13 to shareholders. Looking at the last 12 months of distributions, Elopak has a trailing yield of approximately 4.0% on its current stock price of kr034.95. We love seeing companies pay a dividend, but it's also important to be sure that laying the golden eggs isn't going to kill our golden goose! So we need to investigate whether Elopak can afford its dividend, and if the dividend could grow.

If a company pays out more in dividends than it earned, then the dividend might become unsustainable - hardly an ideal situation. Elopak is paying out an acceptable 66% of its profit, a common payout level among most companies. Yet cash flows are even more important than profits for assessing a dividend, so we need to see if the company generated enough cash to pay its distribution. Thankfully its dividend payments took up just 45% of the free cash flow it generated, which is a comfortable payout ratio.

It's encouraging to see that the dividend is covered by both profit and cash flow. This generally suggests the dividend is sustainable, as long as earnings don't drop precipitously.
